svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "A healthy coronary artery: blood flows freely through a wide lumen."], [1, "The endothelium is damaged. LDL cholesterol enters the artery wall."], [3.5, "Macrophages engulf the cholesterol and become foam cells."], [6, "A plaque (atheroma) grows, with a lipid core and fibrous cap, narrowing the lumen: less blood flows."], [10, "The plaque ruptures and a blood clot (thrombus) forms."], [12.5, "The clot blocks the artery: heart muscle beyond it gets no oxygen and starts to die (heart attack)."]]
svg.title: Coronary heart disease
svg.desc: A longitudinal section of a coronary artery: LDL enters the damaged wall, foam cells form, a plaque with lipid core and fibrous cap narrows the lumen, the plaque ruptures and a clot blocks blood flow, starving heart muscle.
svg.text: Coronary heart disease: atherosclerosis and a heart attack
Longitudinal section through a coronary artery (not to scale).

g.data-info: The space inside the artery where blood flows.
A smooth single layer of cells lining the artery. Damage (from high blood pressure, smoking or high LDL) starts the process.
A lipid core with a fibrous cap. It narrows the lumen and makes the wall less elastic (atherosclerosis).
Low-density lipoprotein enters the damaged wall and builds up.
Macrophages (white blood cells) that have engulfed so much cholesterol that they look foamy.
If the plaque ruptures, platelets and fibrin form a clot that can block the artery completely.
Coronary arteries supply the heart muscle with oxygen and glucose. A blocked artery starves the muscle beyond it: a heart attack (myocardial infarction).
